name_translation: The Yoga of Renunciation of Action

verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
संन्यासं कर्मणां कृष्ण पुनर्योगं च शंससि |
यच्छ्रेय एतयोरेकं तन्मे ब्रूहि सुनिश्चितम् || १ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
saṃnyāsaṃ karmaṇāṃ kṛṣṇa punaryogaṃ ca śaṃsasi |
yacchreya etayorekaṃ tanme brūhi suniścitam || 1 ||
verses.translation: Arjuna said: O Krishna, You praise the renunciation of actions (Sannyasa), and yet again You praise the performance of selfless action (Karma Yoga). Tell me with absolute certainty, which one of these two is definitely superior for my highest good?
verses.meaning: Arjuna is seeking unambiguous practical clarity. Having heard praise for both intellectual renunciation of worldly duties and devoted selfless action, he asks Sri Krishna to declare definitively which path guarantees ultimate spiritual elevation.

verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
संन्यासः कर्मयोगश्च निःश्रेयसकरावुभौ |
तयोस्तु कर्मसंन्यासात्कर्मयोगो विशिष्यते || २ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
saṃnyāsaḥ karmayogaśca niḥśreyasakarāvubhau |
tayostu karmasaṃnyāsātkarmayogo viśiṣyate || 2 ||
verses.translation: The Supreme Lord said: Both the renunciation of action (Sannyasa) and the Yoga of selfless action (Karma Yoga) lead to the supreme goal of liberation. But of the two, the Yoga of selfless action is distinctly superior to mere renunciation of work.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna clarifies that while both paths lead to Moksha, Karma Yoga is far more direct, practical, and purifying for embodied seekers. True renunciation is not abandoning physical duty, but renouncing selfish desires while performing duty.

verses.text_sanskrit:
ज्ञेयः स नित्यसंन्यासी यो न द्वेष्टि न काङ्क्षति |
निर्द्वन्द्वो हि महाबाहो सुखं बन्धात्प्रमुच्यते || ३ ||
verses.transliteration:
jñeyaḥ sa nityasaṃnyāsī yo na dveṣṭi na kāṅkṣati |
nirdvandvo hi mahābāho sukhaṃ bandhātpramucyate || 3 ||
verses.translation: One who neither hates nor desires should be known as a perpetual renunciant (Nitya Sannyasi). Free from all dualities, O mighty-armed Arjuna, such a person is effortlessly liberated from material bondage.
verses.meaning: True sannyasa is an internal state of mind rather than an external orange robe or forest retreat. One who has transcended personal attraction (Raga) and repulsion (Dvesha) lives in perpetual inner renunciation while fulfilling duties in the world.

verses.text_sanskrit:
साङ्ख्ययोगौ पृथग्बालाः प्रवदन्ति न पण्डिताः |
एकमप्यास्थितः सम्यगुभयोर्विन्दते फलम् || ४ ||
verses.transliteration:
sāṅkhyayogau pṛthagbālāḥ pravadanti na paṇḍitāḥ |
ekamapyāsthitaḥ samyagubhayorvindate phalam || 4 ||
verses.translation: Only the immature and uninformed speak of analytical knowledge (Sankhya) and selfless action (Karma Yoga) as being distinct and different; the truly wise do not say so. One who is firmly established in even one of these paths attains the fruit of both.
verses.meaning: Sankhya (contemplative knowledge) and Yoga (selfless action) are two sides of the same spiritual coin. Dedicated practice of either path culminates in the same transcendental realization of freedom and peace.

verses.text_sanskrit:
यत्साङ्ख्यैः प्राप्यते स्थानं तद्योगैरपि गम्यते |
एकं साङ्ख्यं च योगं च यः पश्यति स पश्यति || ५ ||
verses.transliteration:
yatsāṅkhyaiḥ prāpyate sthānaṃ tadyogairapi gamyate |
ekaṃ sāṅkhyaṃ ca yogaṃ ca yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati || 5 ||
verses.translation: The supreme state which is attained by the analytical philosophers (Sankhyas) is also reached by the practitioners of selfless action (Yogis). One who sees Sankhya and Yoga as one and the same truly sees.
verses.meaning: Both philosophical inquiry and selfless action lead to the identical spiritual summit: the direct experience of the immortal Self. True vision recognizes their fundamental unity of purpose.

verses.text_sanskrit:
संन्यासस्तु महाबाहो दुःखमाप्तुमयोगतः |
योगयुक्तो मुनिर्ब्रह्म नचिरेणाधिगच्छति || ६ ||
verses.transliteration:
saṃnyāsastu mahābāho duḥkhamāptumayogataḥ |
yogayukto munirbrahma nacireṇādhigacchati || 6 ||
verses.translation: Renunciation without the practice of Karma Yoga, O mighty-armed Arjuna, is difficult and painful to attain. But the contemplative sage equipped with Karma Yoga quickly attains the Supreme Brahman.
verses.meaning: Attempting renunciation without prior mental purification through selfless service produces inner frustration and cognitive conflict. Karma Yoga cleanses the subconscious mind, allowing effortless elevation into the peace of Brahman.

verses.text_sanskrit:
योगयुक्तो विशुद्धात्मा विजितात्मा जितेन्द्रियः |
सर्वभूतात्मभूतात्मा कुर्वन्नपि न लिप्यते || ७ ||
verses.transliteration:
yogayukto viśuddhātmā vijitātmā jitendriyaḥ |
sarvabhūtātmabhūtātmā kurvannapi na lipyate || 7 ||
verses.translation: One who is harmonized in Yoga, whose intellect is purified, who has mastered the self and conquered the senses, and who sees one's own Self in all living beings—such a person is never tainted, even while performing action.
verses.meaning: The perfected Karma Yogi realizes universal oneness: the divine Self dwelling within one's own heart is the very same Self residing in all creatures. Because egoic doership is dissolved, actions leave no karmic stain.

verses.text_sanskrit:
नैव किञ्चित्करोमीति युक्तो मन्येत तत्त्ववित् |
पश्यञ्शृण्वन्स्पृशञ्जिघ्रन्नश्नन्गच्छन्स्वपञ्श्वसन् || ८ ||
verses.transliteration:
naiva kiñcitkaromīti yukto manyeta tattvavit |
paśyañśṛṇvanspṛśañjighrannaśnangacchansvapañśvasan || 8 ||
verses.translation: The knower of truth, established in Yoga, constantly thinks: 'I do nothing at all,' while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, moving, sleeping, and breathing.
verses.meaning: The enlightened seer (Tattva-vit) remains rooted in the witness consciousness (Sakshi Bhavana), recognizing that physiological and sensory functions are natural operations of the body and mind, while the pure Atman remains untouched.

verses.text_sanskrit:
प्रलपन्विसृजन्गृह्णन्नुन्मिषन्निमिषन्नपि |
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेषु वर्तन्त इति धारयन् || ९ ||
verses.transliteration:
pralapanvisṛjangṛhṇannunmiṣannimiṣannapi |
indriyāṇīndriyārtheṣu vartanta iti dhārayan || 9 ||
verses.translation: Even while speaking, discharging waste, grasping objects, opening or closing the eyes, the wise person remains convinced that: 'It is merely the senses interacting with their respective sense objects.'
verses.meaning: Every mundane bodily act—from blinking to speaking—is understood as the natural interplay of nature's modes (Prakriti). The yogi stays anchored in transcendental detachment.

verses.text_sanskrit:
ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः |
लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा || १० ||
verses.transliteration:
brahmaṇyādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ |
lipyate na sa pāpena padmapatramivāmbhasā || 10 ||
verses.translation: One who performs actions dedicating all works to the Supreme Brahman, completely abandoning selfish attachment, remains untouched by sin, just as a lotus leaf remains untouched and dry upon water.
verses.meaning: One of the most celebrated and beloved analogies in spiritual literature: A lotus leaf grows in muddy water yet water glides off its waxy surface without ever wetting it. Similarly, a devotee performing duties dedicated to God lives in the world completely unaffected by its impurities.

verses.text_sanskrit:
कायेन मनसा बुद्ध्या केवलैरिन्द्रियैरपि |
योगिनः कर्म कुर्वन्ति सङ्गं त्यक्त्वात्मशुद्धये || ११ ||
verses.transliteration:
kāyena manasā buddhyā kevalairindriyairapi |
yoginaḥ karma kurvanti saṅgaṃ tyaktvātmaśuddhaye || 11 ||
verses.translation: Yogis perform action with the physical body, mind, intellect, and even with the senses alone, without selfish attachment, solely for the purpose of self-purification (Atma-shuddhaye).
verses.meaning: Selfless action is the ultimate purifier of consciousness. When physical, mental, and intellectual energy is expended for duty and collective welfare rather than ego-gratification, the inner mirror of the heart becomes pristine.

verses.text_sanskrit:
युक्तः कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम् |
अयुक्तः कामकारेण फले सक्तो निबध्यते || १२ ||
verses.transliteration:
yuktaḥ karmaphalaṃ tyaktvā śāntimāpnoti naiṣṭhikīm |
ayuktaḥ kāmakāreṇa phale sakto nibadhyate || 12 ||
verses.translation: The devoted practitioner, abandoning attachment to the fruits of action, attains everlasting transcendental peace. But the undisciplined one, driven by selfish craving, attached to results, becomes bound.
verses.meaning: Inner peace is the immediate consequence of detachment. Anxiety and bondage do not come from the work we perform, but from obsessive clinging to future results and personal expectations.

verses.text_sanskrit:
सर्वकर्माणि मनसा संन्यस्यास्ते सुखं वशी |
नवद्वारे पुरे देही नैव कुर्वन्न कारयन् || १३ ||
verses.transliteration:
sarvakarmāṇi manasā saṃnyasyāste sukhaṃ vaśī |
navadvāre pure dehī naiva kurvanna kārayan || 13 ||
verses.translation: The self-controlled embodied soul, mentally renouncing all actions, resides happily within the city of nine gates (the physical body), neither acting nor causing others to act.
verses.meaning: The physical body is poetically depicted as a fortress with nine gates (two eyes, two ears, two nostrils, mouth, and two lower organs). The self-realized master resides peacefully inside this city as the serene, sovereign witness.

verses.text_sanskrit:
न कर्तृत्वं न कर्माणि लोकस्य सृजति प्रभुः |
न कर्मफलसंयोगं स्वभावस्तु प्रवर्तते || १४ ||
verses.transliteration:
na kartṛtvaṃ na karmāṇi lokasya sṛjati prabhuḥ |
na karmaphalasaṃyogaṃ svabhāvastu pravartate || 14 ||
verses.translation: The Supreme Lord creates neither agency (doership), nor actions, nor the union of action with its fruit for the people; it is innate nature (Svabhava / Prakriti) that operates.
verses.meaning: The Divine is the non-interfering, impartial consciousness of existence. Human actions, tendencies, and desires flow from the conditioning of material nature (Svabhava). The soul's true nature is transcendental freedom.

verses.text_sanskrit:
नादत्ते कस्यचित्पापं न चैव सुकृतं विभुः |
अज्ञानेनावृतं ज्ञानं तेन मुह्यन्ति जन्तवः || १५ ||
verses.transliteration:
nādatte kasyacitpāpaṃ na caiva sukṛtaṃ vibhuḥ |
ajñānenāvṛtaṃ jñānaṃ tena muhyanti jantavaḥ || 15 ||
verses.translation: The all-pervading Supreme Lord takes on neither the sins nor the merits of anyone. Spiritual wisdom is covered by the darkness of ignorance, and thereby living beings are deluded.
verses.meaning: God does not arbitrary dispense punishment or reward; karmic law operates systematically. Suffering arises because spiritual ignorance (Ajnana) veils the innate divinity within, causing egoic attachment and sorrow.

verses.text_sanskrit:
ज्ञानेन तु तदज्ञानं येषां नाशितमात्मनः |
तेषामादित्यवज्ज्ञानं प्रकाशयति तत्परम् || १६ ||
verses.transliteration:
jñānena tu tadajñānaṃ yeṣāṃ nāśitamātmanaḥ |
teṣāmādityavajjñānaṃ prakāśayati tatparam || 16 ||
verses.translation: But for those whose ignorance of the Self has been destroyed by spiritual knowledge, that supreme wisdom, like the brilliant sun, illuminates the transcendental Supreme Reality.
verses.meaning: Just as the morning sun dispels the thickest darkness, Self-knowledge instantly eradicates the illusion of separation, revealing the ever-present, radiant divinity of Brahman within and without.

verses.text_sanskrit:
तद्बुद्धयस्तदात्मानस्तन्निष्ठास्तत्परायणाः |
गच्छन्त्यपुनरावृत्तिं ज्ञाननिर्धूतकल्मषाः || १७ ||
verses.transliteration:
tadbuddhayastadātmānastanniṣṭhāstatparāyaṇāḥ |
gacchantyapunarāvṛttiṃ jñānanirdhūtakalmaṣāḥ || 17 ||
verses.translation: Those whose intellect is fixed on the Supreme, whose very soul is absorbed in the Divine, who are steadfast in That, and have That as their ultimate refuge, reach the state from which there is no return, their sins cleansed by knowledge.
verses.meaning: When intellect, identity, devotion, and daily aspirations are unified in God, all karmic dross is washed away. The soul attains the supreme liberation of non-return (Apunaravritti).

verses.text_sanskrit:
विद्याविनयसम्पन्ने ब्राह्मणे गवि हस्तिनि |
शुनि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः || १८ ||
verses.transliteration:
vidyāvinayasampanne brāhmaṇe gavi hastini |
śuni caiva śvapāke ca paṇḍitāḥ samadarśinaḥ || 18 ||
verses.translation: The truly enlightened sages look with equal vision (Sama-darshana) upon a learned and humble scholar, a cow, an elephant, a dog, and an outcaste.
verses.meaning: One of the most foundational ethical verses of the Gita. Enlightened seers look past external bodily costumes, species, social statuses, and appearances to perceive the exact same divine spark of Brahman glowing within all living entities.

verses.text_sanskrit:
इहैव तैर्जितः सर्गो येषां साम्ये स्थितं मनः |
निर्दोषं हि समं ब्रह्म तस्माद्ब्रह्मणि ते स्थिताः || १९ ||
verses.transliteration:
ihaiva tairjitaḥ sargo yeṣāṃ sāmye sthitaṃ manaḥ |
nirdoṣaṃ hi samaṃ brahma tasmādbrahmaṇi te sthitāḥ || 19 ||
verses.translation: Even here in this physical world, the cycle of birth and death is conquered by those whose minds are established in equanimity. Since Brahman is flawless and equanimous, they are already established in Brahman.
verses.meaning: Liberation is not merely a post-mortem promise; it is attainable right here and now (Ihaiva). A mind rooted in flawless balance mirrors the attribute of Brahman and abides continuously in the Divine.

verses.text_sanskrit:
न प्रहृष्येत्प्रियं प्राप्य नोद्विजेत्प्राप्य चाप्रियम् |
स्थिरबुद्धिरसंमूढो ब्रह्मविद्ब्रह्मणि स्थितः || २० ||
verses.transliteration:
na prahṛṣyetpriyaṃ prāpya nodvijetprāpya cāpriyam |
sthirabuddhirasaṃmūḍho brahmavidbrahmaṇi sthitaḥ || 20 ||
verses.translation: One who neither rejoices upon obtaining what is pleasant nor grieves upon encountering what is unpleasant, possessing steady intellect, free from delusion—such a knower of Brahman is established in Brahman.
verses.meaning: The hallmark of the Brahmavid (knower of Brahman) is emotional poise. Neither elated by worldly fortune nor depressed by adversity, the sage abides in unshakable tranquility.

verses.text_sanskrit:
बाह्यस्पर्शेष्वसक्तात्मा विन्दत्यात्मनि यत्सुखम् |
स ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा सुखमक्षय्यमश्नुते || २१ ||
verses.transliteration:
bāhyasparśeṣvasaktātmā vindatyātmani yatsukham |
sa brahmayogayuktātmā sukhamakṣayyamaśnute || 21 ||
verses.translation: One whose consciousness is unattached to external sensory contacts discovers the joy residing in the Self. Being united in union with Brahman (Brahma-yoga), such a soul enjoys inexhaustible bliss (Akshaya Sukham).
verses.meaning: Sensory pleasures are fleeting and shallow. When the mind turns inward and unites with the infinite consciousness of Brahman, it experiences an inexhaustible, ever-renewing fountain of supreme bliss.

verses.text_sanskrit:
ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते |
आद्यन्तवन्तः कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुधः || २२ ||
verses.transliteration:
ye hi saṃsparśajā bhogā duḥkhayonaya eva te |
ādyantavantaḥ kaunteya na teṣu ramate budhaḥ || 22 ||
verses.translation: The pleasures born of sensory contact are indeed the veritable breeding grounds of suffering; for they have a beginning and an end, O son of Kunti. The wise person does not delight in them.
verses.meaning: Sensual gratifications carry the seeds of disappointment, addiction, and sorrow because they are ephemeral (Adyantavantah). The wise seek the permanent fulfillment of the spirit rather than transient sensory thrills.

verses.text_sanskrit:
शक्नोतीहैव यः सोढुं प्राक्शरीरविमोक्षणात् |
कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः || २३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śaknotīhaiva yaḥ soḍhuṃ prākśarīravimokṣaṇāt |
kāmakrodhodbhavaṃ vegaṃ sa yuktaḥ sa sukhī naraḥ || 23 ||
verses.translation: One who is able to withstand the turbulent surges of desire and anger here in this world, before departing from the physical body—that person is a true yogi; that person is truly happy.
verses.meaning: Real heroism is internal mastery. Withstanding the violent psychological impulses (Vega) of lust and rage before death seals one's spiritual triumph and bestows genuine, lasting happiness.

verses.text_sanskrit:
योऽन्तःसुखोऽन्तरारामस्तथान्तर्ज्योतिरेव यः |
स योगी ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं ब्रह्मभूतोऽधिगच्छति || २४ ||
verses.transliteration:
yo'ntaḥsukho'ntarāramastathāntarjyotireva yaḥ |
sa yogī brahmanirvāṇaṃ brahmabhūto'dhigacchati || 24 ||
verses.translation: One who finds inner happiness, who rejoices within, and who is illuminated by the inner light—that yogi, having attained oneness with Brahman, attains liberation in the Supreme (Brahman-nirvana).
verses.meaning: The triple mark of self-realization: Antah-sukha (inner joy), Antar-arama (inner contentment), and Antar-jyoti (inner illumination). Such a sage experiences Brahman-nirvana—complete spiritual liberation.

verses.text_sanskrit:
लभन्ते ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृषयः क्षीणकल्मषाः |
छिन्नद्वैधा यतात्मानः सर्वभूतहिते रताः || २५ ||
verses.transliteration:
labhante brahmanirvāṇamṛṣayaḥ kṣīṇakalmaṣāḥ |
chinnadvaidhā yatātmānaḥ sarvabhūtahite ratāḥ || 25 ||
verses.translation: The holy seers attain liberation in Brahman—those whose sins are extinguished, whose doubts are resolved, whose minds are self-controlled, and who are actively engaged in the welfare of all living beings (Sarva-bhuta-hite ratah).
verses.meaning: Enlightenment expresses itself as universal compassion. A genuine sage does not remain indifferent, but actively rejoices in and contributes to the well-being and upliftment of all creatures.

verses.text_sanskrit:
कामक्रोधवियुक्तानां यतीनां यतचेतसाम् |
अभितो ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं वर्तते विदितात्मनाम् || २६ ||
verses.transliteration:
kāmakrodhaviyuktānāṃ yatīnāṃ yatacetasām |
abhito brahmanirvāṇaṃ vartate viditātmanām || 26 ||
verses.translation: For those self-disciplined seekers who are free from desire and anger, whose minds are controlled, and who have realized the Self, liberation in Brahman is present all around them, both here and hereafter.
verses.meaning: Liberation surrounds the master like an all-encompassing atmosphere (Abhitah). Having dissolved inner desires and realized their true nature, they dwell in the eternal peace of Brahman at all times.

verses.text_sanskrit:
स्पर्शान्कृत्वा बहिर्बाह्यांश्चक्षुश्चैवान्तरे भ्रुवोः |
प्राणापानौ समौ कृत्वा नासाभ्यन्तरचारिणौ || २७ ||
verses.transliteration:
sparśānkṛtvā bahirbāhyāṃścakṣuścaivāntare bhruvoḥ |
prāṇāpānau samau kṛtvā nāsābhyantaracāriṇau || 27 ||
verses.translation: Shutting out all external sensory contacts, fixing the gaze between the eyebrows, balancing the incoming (Prana) and outgoing (Apana) breaths moving through the nostrils...
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna provides an evocative prelude to the science of meditation (Dhyana Yoga, to be elaborated in Chapter 6): sensory withdrawal, gentle gaze stabilization (Ajna Chakra focus), and rhythmic breath equalization.

verses.text_sanskrit:
यतेन्द्रियमनोबुद्धिर्मुनिर्मोक्षपरायणः |
विगतेच्छाभयक्रोधो यः सदा मुक्त एव सः || २८ ||
verses.transliteration:
yatendriyamanobuddhirmunirmokṣaparāyaṇaḥ |
vigatecchābhayakrodho yaḥ sadā mukta eva saḥ || 28 ||
verses.translation: ...with the senses, mind, and intellect fully controlled, the contemplative sage dedicated to liberation, forever free from desire, fear, and anger, is indeed eternally liberated.
verses.meaning: The culmination of yogic meditation: When intellect, mind, and senses are unified in contemplation and emptied of fear, craving, and hostility, the soul experiences perpetual freedom (Sada mukta eva sah).

verses.text_sanskrit:
भोक्तारं यज्ञतपसां सर्वलोकमहेश्वरम् |
सुहृदं सर्वभूतानां ज्ञात्वा मां शान्तिमृच्छति || २९ ||
verses.transliteration:
bhoktāraṃ yajñatapasāṃ sarvalokamaheśvaram |
suhṛdaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ jñātvā māṃ śāntimṛcchati || 29 ||
verses.translation: Knowing Me as the ultimate beneficiary and enjoyer of all sacrifices and austerities, the Supreme Sovereign of all the worlds, and the intimate, benevolent friend of all living beings, one attains supreme transcendental peace.
verses.meaning: The glorious Shanti-Mantra climax of Chapter 5. Sri Krishna reveals His divine identity as the supreme Enjoyer (Bhokta), the Lord of all creation (Maheshvara), and the ever-compassionate, loving friend (Suhridam) residing in every heart. Realizing this intimate truth unlocks infinite peace.
